$comment: The 'validate' feature (custom validation callback on flags) is expressed through the closed `validate` vocabulary on a flag entry (a reject list plus a message) rather than as an arbitrary callable: a JSON case cannot carry a function, but it can carry the one shape the conformance corpus needs -- a validator that refuses named values -- and each harness builds the identical callable from it. Richer validators stay in the per-language unit suites.
title: strictcli conformance test cases
description: Array of test cases for verifying strictcli implementations.

skip_schema_validation.description: If true, this test case is exempt from schema validation (used for cases that intentionally craft invalid app definitions).

targets.description: Restrict which implementations run this case. Absent means all. Used for cases that are only expressible in some languages (e.g. the bad-return hard error, expressible in Python and TypeScript but unrepresentable in Go's type system).

reason.description: Why the acknowledged targets' output is intentionally language-specific (parser prose, tracebacks, idiomatic API names). Mandatory audit trail.

acknowledged_divergence.description: Declares targets whose output on a stream intentionally differs from the rest. The N-way parity runner excludes them from that stream's byte-identity comparison; each target's own expect block still runs unchanged. Double-entry: if an acknowledged target's output does not actually differ, the runner reports a stale-acknowledgment divergence warning. At least one applicable target per stream must remain unacknowledged as the comparison baseline.

env.description: Environment variables to set before invoking the app.

stdin.description: Text piped to the app's stdin. Absent means /dev/null, which is what keeps every other case independent of the operator's terminal; a pipe carrying this text is not a TTY either. Used by the --mcp cases, whose JSON-RPC lines arrive on stdin.

protocol_script.description: A line-scripted request/response exchange with the running app, for protocols whose next request depends on the previous reply -- the MCP loop and its confirmation round-trip above all. The runner sends each step's line, then reads and asserts one reply line, step by step; the child's full streams are still available to the ordinary expect block and to the N-way comparison. Mutually exclusive with 'stdin', which hands the whole input over up front and can only express an exchange that never reacts.

protocol_step.description: One step of a line-scripted exchange: send a line, and/or read and assert one reply line. A step with only 'send' does not wait; a step with only 'expect_line' or 'capture' reads without sending.

send.description: The line written to the child's stdin. The terminating newline is added by the runner. A '{{name}}' placeholder splices in a value an earlier step captured, and '{{name|tamper}}' splices it with its FIRST character changed -- which is how a case asserts that an integrity-protected value is actually checked. The first character and not the last, because base64 decoders ignore the trailing bits of a final character that does not fill a byte, so changing the last character of a base64url blob can decode to the identical bytes.

capture.description: Values to pull out of this step's reply for later steps to splice into what they send, as {name: dotted path into the parsed reply}. This is the only way to script a protocol whose later requests quote something the server minted -- a continuation state blob, say, which is unguessable by construction and different every run. A step carrying 'capture' reads a reply line even when it asserts nothing about it.

stream.description: Which of the child's streams the reply line is read from.

expect_line.description: Assertions on the one reply line this step reads (its trailing newline stripped). A missing line within the step timeout is a failure, never a hang.

json_equals.description: Parse the line as JSON and compare it structurally against this document -- key order and encoder whitespace are therefore not part of the assertion, which is exactly what makes one expectation serve three different serializers. '$ANY' is the per-field wildcard, for a value that is nondeterministic by construction.

config.description: If true, enable config file support and auto-register config subcommands.

config_path.description: Override the default config file path. If null, uses XDG_CONFIG_HOME/<app>/config.<format>.

schema_path.description: Where --dump-schema writes. Absolute, or relative to the app's construction-time working directory. If null, the framework's own location applies: .strictcli/schema.json anchored at that same directory.

global_flags.description: Flags declared on the App, parsed before the command name and available to every handler.

checks_path.description: Override CWD-based discovery of checks.toml with an explicit path.

no_default_config_path.description: If true, the app loads no config unless --config is explicitly passed.

config_conflict_mode.description: Conflict resolution mode for config values. In 'error' mode, config+cli and config+env overlaps are hard errors.

infra_root.description: Infrastructure location roots: env var name -> default path. Resolved eagerly at construction; immune to --hermetic.

handshake_env.description: Handshake env vars: env var name -> help string. Read live at access time via the infra accessor.

connection_env.description: Connection env vars: env var name -> help string. Hermetic-suppressed, read live at access time, no default.

confirm_stdin_interactive.description: Installs the framework's test-only confirm seam (Go App.SetConfirmIO, Python App._set_confirm_io, TypeScript setConfirmIO) so the confirm protocol treats the case's piped stdin as interactive and reads its answer from it. Without this the interactive branch is unreachable from a subprocess -- a pipe is not a TTY in any implementation, so every consequential case would take the non-interactive error branch. It changes WHERE the answer comes from, never WHETHER the protocol runs: there is no bypass here.

config_content.description: Raw config file content to write before running the test

config_content_late.description: Raw config file content to write AFTER app construction but BEFORE app.run(). Tests parse-time config loading vs construction-time.

checks_toml.description: Raw TOML content to write as .strictcli/checks.toml for check conformance tests.

checks.description: Check stub definitions for code generation.

providers.description: Check providers registered via register_check_provider / RegisterCheckProvider. Each element is one provider (a list of the specs it returns). Providers have no TOML, so every spec carries its declarative meta inline.

test_coverage.description: Enable CLI test-coverage instrumentation. When true, every test() call records the command path, and a cli-test-coverage check is auto-registered.

pre_test.description: List of argv lists to run via app.test() before the main app.run(). Used by test_coverage cases to generate shard files.

command.description: Dot-separated command path to invoke programmatically.

kwargs.description: Pre-typed handler kwargs, keyed by underscored parameter name.

approve_consequential.description: The caller's explicit consent, spelled per-language (Python keyword-only argument, Go CallOption, TS options object). Absent means no consent, so a consequential command is refused.

pre_call.description: Programmatic calls to run via app.call()/App.Call() before the main app.run(). Each prints 'call ok: <command>' to stdout, or 'call error: <message>' to stderr when the call is refused. The argv-and-subprocess harness cannot otherwise reach the programmatic channel.

dump_tools.description: Print one 'tool: <name> effect=<effect> consequential=<bool>' line per as_tools()/AsTools() descriptor to stdout before the main app.run(). Pins the exported classification without serializing the whole descriptor, whose JSON shape is language-specific.

coverage_manifest.description: Committed coverage manifest to seed at run_cwd/.strictcli/test-coverage.json before the app runs. Used by test_coverage cases to exercise the deterministic manifest-union verdict on the empty-shard path (no pre_test).

config_fields_def.description: Config field definitions registered on the app via app.config_field() / app.ConfigField().

proc_observe_allowlist.description: App-level observe authorization (effects contract §6.2): argv PREFIXES matched element-wise by string equality. A ctx.effects.run whose argv matches one is an observe -- it executes even in dry mode, returns a real value, and is never written to the would-do log.

check.description: A check-impl stub for code generation. The registration form (error vs warn) is NOT specified here -- generators derive it from the check's severity in the embedded checks_toml. This object only describes what the impl mints via its reporter -- or, with 'aborts', that it mints nothing and unwinds instead.

aborts.description: The check impl ABORTS instead of returning an outcome: it raises (Python), throws (TypeScript) or panics (Go) a harness-defined type named CheckAborted carrying the identical message 'conformance: check aborted'. The three type names coincide by construction, so the framework's containment line (which names the type) is byte-identical across targets. Only true is declarable, and it excludes mint / message / problems / notes: an aborting impl mints nothing.
aborts.$comment: The check analog of a command's handler_aborts.

mint.description: Which terminal outcome the reporter mints. 'found' requires at least one problem; 'passed'/'skipped' forbid problems.

message.description: The pass/found message or skip reason passed to reporter.passed/found/skipped.

problems.description: Problems the reporter mints before found(). Only valid when mint == 'found'. A warn-severity check may only mint 'warn' problems.

notes.description: Verdict-inert informational notes the reporter records via note()/Note(). They surface only under --verbose and in JSON, on any outcome including a pass.

provider_check.description: A provider-sourced check spec. Unlike a TOML-declared check, it carries all eight declarative meta fields inline (providers have no TOML). The impl body (mint/message/problems) mirrors a 'check' def. 'impl_form' selects the constructor (error_check_spec / warn_check_spec); when it differs from 'severity', it pins the materialization-time severity-mismatch hard error.

impl_form.description: Which constructor registers the spec. Defaults to 'severity'. A value differing from 'severity' pins the severity-mismatch hard error.

mint.description: Which terminal outcome the reporter mints.

notes.description: Verdict-inert informational notes the reporter records via note()/Note().

effect.description: The mandatory command classification (effects contract §1.1). Deliberately NOT in the top-level 'required' list: a top-level required applies conjunctively with the deprecated branch's 'then', which would make classification mandatory on deprecated entries too -- the opposite of §1.1's exemption. The 'else' branch below is what makes it mandatory on every non-deprecated entry.

consequential.description: Declares that the command's effects are worth interrupting someone for (effects contract §8.1). The framework prompts for exactly these commands and for no others. NOT mandatory -- absence means 'not consequential' -- so it is neither in 'required' nor in the 'else' branch. Declaring it on a read_only command is a registration-time hard error.

dry_run_supported.description: Declares whether --dry-run is honored for this command. Only false is declarable: true is the regime's baseline (a mutating command's effects are recorded rather than executed). A command that declares false is saying a preview of it would misrepresent the real run, so the framework refuses --dry-run for it at parse time. NOT mandatory -- absence means supported -- so it is neither in 'required' nor in the 'else' branch. Declaring false on a read_only command is a registration-time hard error, and it requires dry_run_unsupported_reason.

payload_schema.description: The command's machine payload contract (effects contract §19.5): an inline JSON Schema literal, registered as written, validated at registration over the closed subset, enforced against the payload at emission, and published verbatim by --dump-schema. Absence means the command cannot produce a payload -- ctx.payload is then a call-time hard error. Most cases leave this key out: the harnesses declare the permissive literal {} for every command whose handler_returns supplies a payload, identically in all three languages. Write it explicitly when the case is ABOUT the declaration -- a non-empty literal published by the schema dump, or a payload validated against real keywords.

owns_stdout.description: Declares that this command's stdout IS the artifact (effects contract §19.6): in machine mode stdout carries the command's own document byte-exactly and the envelope moves to stderr, together with every framework diagnostic it carries. Outside machine mode the declaration changes nothing at all. Emitted by --dump-schema only when true; absence means the framework owns stdout, which is the baseline.

dry_run_unsupported_reason.description: Why a dry run of this command would misrepresent the real run. Mandatory when dry_run_supported is false, and illegal without it. Shown in the command's help and repeated in the parse-time refusal.

forwarding.description: Declared forwarding (effects contract §10.2). The reason is mandatory and non-empty.

handler_effects.description: Effect calls the generated handler issues, in order, before its return (effects contract §14.4). Runs BEFORE the handler_prints / handler_returns path and does not replace it.

handler_diagnostics.description: Context diagnostic calls the generated handler issues, in order, after its handler_effects and before the handler_prints / handler_returns path.

handler_claims_log.description: The generated handler calls ctx.effects.recorded() (effects contract §19.7), which CLAIMS the render: the framework's own end-of-dispatch emission is suppressed for the rest of the run. A claim that never renders is re-rendered at the seam, so this key alone changes no output -- it exists to pin exactly that. Runs after handler_effects and before handler_diagnostics / handler_prints.

handler_renders_log.description: The generated handler calls ctx.effects.render_log() / RenderLog() / renderLog() (effects contract §19.7), which renders the would-do log in §3.2's exact form at that point in the handler body and claims the render. Runs after handler_effects and before handler_diagnostics / handler_prints, so the log lands AHEAD of the handler's own output. A no-op in machine mode and outside dry mode.

handler_payloads_recorded.description: The generated handler calls ctx.payload with the verbs of ctx.effects.recorded() (effects contract §19.7): the records it reads shape its own payload, identically in both modes. The verbs rather than the records themselves, because a payload is emitted exactly as the handler supplied it (§19.2) and three serializers order an object's keys three ways -- an array of strings is the same bytes everywhere. Implies the permissive payload_schema literal {} when the command declares none.

deprecated.description: If true, this is a deprecated command. It must have deprecated_message and must NOT have handler_prints, handler_exit_code, flags, args, flag_sets, mutex, dependencies, passthrough, or passthrough_handler_prints.

deprecated_message.description: Deprecation message shown when the command is invoked or listed in help. Required when deprecated is true.

handler_prints.description: Template string. {name} is replaced with the value of the arg/flag named 'name'; {source:name} is replaced with the provenance source label via ctx.source(name).

handler_exit_code.description: The integer value the generated handler returns (as outcome(exit_code=N) / Exit(N)). Used as the process exit code.

handler_returns.description: Pins an explicit handler return (survivor-contract cases). When present, the template-printing path is skipped. 'exit' => outcome(exit_code)/Exit(code); 'data' => ctx.payload(data) then outcome()/Exit(0); 'exit_data' => ctx.payload(data) then outcome(exit_code)/Exit(code); 'none' => return None (Python)/Exit(0) (Go)/return undefined (TypeScript); 'bad' => an invalid return (a hard error on Python and TypeScript; Go's type system makes it unrepresentable, so a 'bad' case must exclude the go target). The data kinds require the command to declare a payload_schema (contract §19.4).

data.description: Structured data payload for data/exit_data kinds. Author with sorted keys so compact JSON is byte-identical across languages.

handler_aborts.description: The generated handler ABORTS instead of returning: it raises (Python), throws (TypeScript) or panics (Go) with the identical message 'conformance: handler aborted', after running its handler_effects and handler_diagnostics. This is the language-neutral way to reach the framework's unwinding paths (the aborted-preview marker, effects contract §12.3) -- unlike handler_returns kind 'bad', which Go's Outcome type makes unrepresentable. Only true is declarable, and it excludes handler_returns: an aborting handler has no return.

passthrough.description: If true, the command is a passthrough command: no flag/arg parsing, handler receives raw args.

passthrough_handler_prints.description: Template for passthrough handler output. Receives name and raw args. Generated handler prints name:arg1,arg2,...

grant.description: A per-command, per-effect-kind authorization with a mandatory human reason (effects contract §6.1).

handler_effect.description: One effect call the generated handler issues (effects contract §14.4). Each harness materializes this identically: iterate in order, call the named method with EXACTLY the keys the entry declares (no per-method filtering -- a case declaring a key the method does not accept is asserting the error), and keep the returned carrier in a per-run slice indexed by position so forward_from / extract_from can reference it.

forward_from.description: 1-based index of an earlier handler_effects entry whose carrier is forwarded as the final argument of this call.

extract_from.description: 1-based index of an earlier entry whose carrier the handler EXTRACTS from (bool-tests it), triggering the truncation path. Terminal: nothing after this entry runs.

handler_diagnostic.description: One Context diagnostic call the generated handler issues. The four levels are gated by --quiet / --verbose per the effects contract §7.4: debug is hidden unless --verbose, info is hidden under --quiet, and warn / error are never suppressed. Each harness materializes this identically: iterate in order, call ctx.debug / ctx.info / ctx.warn / ctx.error with the declared message.

effect_record.description: One record of the structured effect log (effects contract §14.2). Populated in BOTH modes; 'recorded' is the key that says which happened.

allOf.$comment: Contract §23.1/§23.3: `default` co-occurs exactly with presence="default". A case that spells an illegal combination (to assert a registration error) declares skip_schema_validation.

presence.description: The presence declaration (contract §23.3). Exactly one of the three facts, on every declared arg. `default` is spelled by the `default` key beside presence="default".

variadic.description: If true, collects all remaining positional args into a list. Must be the last declared arg.

allOf.$comment: Contract §23.1: `default` (or its RelativeToRoot marker form) co-occurs exactly with presence="default". A case that spells an illegal combination (to assert a registration error) declares skip_schema_validation.

presence.description: The presence declaration (contract §23.1, §23.2). Exactly one of the three facts, on every declared flag at every level. `default` is spelled by the `default` key (or `default_relative_to_root`) beside presence="default".

oneOf.$comment: A dict flag's declared default (contract §23.5's dict row). Values are scalars matching the flag's value type.

default_relative_to_root.description: Flag default that resolves through a declared infra root (RelativeToRoot marker).

negatable.description: Whether --no-flagname negation is supported. Only meaningful for bool-type flags.

conflict_mode.description: Per-flag override of the app config conflict mode. Absent means inherit the app-level config_conflict_mode.

validate.description: A custom validation callback (ValidateFn / validate=), expressed as a closed vocabulary a JSON case can carry: the listed values are rejected with the given message, everything else passes. Each harness builds the same callable, so the resulting `--<flag>: <message>` parse error is byte-identical across targets. Contract §23.5's validate row -- it runs on a supplied value only, never on a declared default.

exit_code_by_target.description: Per-target override of exit_code, for a status that is intrinsically the language's own rather than the framework's. The only such status today is an unrecovered crash: effects contract §3.5 leaves an unwinding dispatch's exit status to the language ('whatever the language would have produced anyway'), and an unrecovered Go panic exits 2 where an uncaught Python exception and an uncaught Node throw both exit 1. It overrides ONLY the status: the case stays a single case and its stdout and stderr are still compared byte-for-byte across every target.

stdout_contains.description: Substring(s) that must appear in stdout.

stdout_matches.description: Regex pattern(s) that must match (re.search) somewhere in stdout. For non-deterministic content like durations.

stderr_matches.description: Regex pattern(s) that must match (re.search) somewhere in stderr.

stderr_contains.description: Substring(s) that must appear in stderr.

stdout_not_contains.description: Substring(s) that must NOT appear in stdout.

stderr_not_contains.description: Substring(s) that must NOT appear in stderr.

config_file_contains.description: Substring(s) that must appear in the seeded config file after the run (reads the config_content / config_content_late temp file).

config_file_not_contains.description: Substring(s) that must NOT appear in the seeded config file after the run.

config_file_matches.description: Regex pattern(s) that must match (re.search) somewhere in the seeded config file after the run. Useful for asserting key ordering.

effects_equals.description: Deep-equality assertion against the structured effect log the run produced (effects contract §14.1). Comparison is STRUCTURAL over the parsed JSON arrays, in order: key order is never compared, key sets are compared as sets (failing fast on the first difference), and values recurse. Absent optional keys and explicit-null keys are equivalent. 'recorded' is required on every record and is therefore never absent. An expected value of the string '$ANY' matches any actual value of any type -- the per-field wildcard for a field whose value is nondeterministic by construction (a continuation signature, a timestamp), where the contract is that the field is present, not what it holds.

schema_command_keys.description: Per-command key assertions against the .strictcli/schema.json a --dump-schema run emitted. Maps a dotted command path (groups then command, e.g. 'release.run') to the keys that entry must carry, with their expected values. Values are compared structurally by the same comparator effects_equals uses, so '$ANY' is the per-field wildcard here too: it asserts the key's presence and nothing about its content. Requires --dump-schema in the case argv.

schema_command_absent_keys.description: The mirror of schema_command_keys: maps a dotted command path to keys that must NOT appear on that entry. Pins the emit-when-declared contract (a key omitted by one implementation and emitted with a default value by another is a silent divergence). Requires --dump-schema in the case argv.
